source: Silva, Feng, Foster (2015) Trajectory events across hippocampal place-cells require previous experience
finding: Failed replication of preplay. Pre-experience sleep events were not temporally correlated with later place-field order, using the same Spearman-rank method as the original preplay papers.
numbers: 4 rats, 40 tetrodes, mean 61 place cells per epoch, 3 novel linear tracks per day. Sleep 1: 9803 candidate events; absolute rank correlation median 0.174 real vs 0.172 shuffled (rank-sum p=0.08, KS p=0.122, Levene p=0.44). Best-template method: 0.245 vs 0.258 (p=1).
quote: absence of temporally sequenced events prior to experience
limits: Linear tracks only, CA1 only, 4 rats.
agent_relevance: A sequence that looks like a plan may be a statistics artifact. Test structure against a matched shuffle before crediting it.

source: Silva, Feng, Foster (2015) Trajectory events across hippocampal place-cells require previous experience
finding: Same data: 'trajectory events' were defined by two joint thresholds (weighted correlation and max jump distance). Run events pass, Sleep-1 events fail, for all three novel tracks. One threshold alone gives spurious significance.
numbers: Sleep 1 (9818 events) vs Run 1 (4438): abs weighted correlation 0.17 vs 0.40; max jump 0.75 vs 0.43; replay score 1.00 vs 0.27; sharpness 0.19 vs 0.26; all p<1e-10. Poisson-rate and time-swap controls reproduced the spurious single-threshold pattern in Sleep 1. 86% of candidate events occurred in the end fifths of the track.
limits: Decoder thresholds are analyst choices.
agent_relevance: Use at least two independent criteria (coherence and no large jumps) to call a chain a plan. One criterion alone yields false positives.

source: Silva, Feng, Foster (2015) Trajectory events across hippocampal place-cells require previous experience
finding: NMDA-receptor blockade during novel runs abolished trajectory events but left place fields mostly intact. Experience-dependent plasticity builds replay; it is not purely pre-wired.
numbers: D-CPPene before Runs 2 and 3: saline Runs 2 and 3 significant for trajectory events, drug Runs 2 and 3 not. Decoding error rose (Kruskal-Wallis H(2)=3270.74, p<1e-10), but adding matched noise to saline spikes still gave clear trajectories, so degraded decoding did not explain the loss. Retrieval of Run 1 events after drug was preserved.
limits: Systemic drug, so non-hippocampal effects possible. 4 rats.
agent_relevance: Learning a sequence and replaying it are separate steps. A scaffold should store traces during a task, not assume they exist beforehand.

source: Silva, Feng, Foster (2015) Trajectory events across hippocampal place-cells require previous experience
finding: Silva argues the original preplay shuffle was unimodal while the real distribution was bimodal, which is inconsistent with picking the best template per event. That is the specific statistical flaw alleged.
numbers: With best-template selection applied to both real and shuffled data, both histograms were bimodal (median 0.245 vs 0.258, p=1). Results held after subsampling cells to original-report numbers and after L-ratio quality screens (435/442 units, 98%, well clustered).
limits: Authors' reading of the original Methods.
agent_relevance: Matched procedures between data and null are required before any claim of a plan-like sequence.

source: Davidson, Kloosterman, Wilson (2009) Hippocampal replay of extended experience
finding: On a 10.3 m track, long replay events (over 250 ms) represent long stretches of the track. Replay is not limited to the local neighbourhood or to a single short ripple.
numbers: 4 rats with 47, 34, 23, 32 units. Candidate-event rate 0.36, 0.40, 0.32, 0.40 per s during stops. 19% of events (17, 22, 16, 14% by rat) were over 250 ms; durations 40-1018 ms.
limits: Rats not pretrained; behaviour variable. Decoder choice matters.
agent_relevance: Long, multi-step replays suggest chaining many steps in one pass. Plans are not limited to one-step lookahead.

source: Olafsdottir, Barry, Saleem, Hassabis, Spiers (2015) Hippocampal place cells construct reward related sequences through unexplored space
finding: Positive preplay result under a boundary condition. Place cells at rest, before first access to a visible arm, fired in the order of the baited arm, but not for the similar unrewarded arm.
numbers: 4 rats on a T-track with a see-through barrier. After goal-cueing, mean bias toward the cued arm 0.33; before cueing, two rats preferred the uncued side (mean bias 0.10).
quote: not observed for an unrewarded but otherwise similar portion of the environment
limits: 4 animals. Preplay tied to motivational relevance and visual access. Could be fast construction from visual input, not pre-existing structure.
agent_relevance: Offline preview of unexplored options appears only for goal-relevant ones. Prune imagined branches by goal relevance.

source: Breffle, Germaine, Shin, Jadhav, Miller (2024) Intrinsic dynamics of randomly clustered networks generate place fields and preplay of novel environments
finding: A random clustered-connectivity network produces preplay of novel tracks with no pre-configured maps. Preplay quality peaks in a small-world regime (high clustering, short paths). The same analyses applied to published rat data (first W-track exposure) also gave above-shuffle events.
numbers: Estimated capacity about 8.6 tracks for the fiducial parameters, vs about 15 tracks reported by Dragoi and Tonegawa 2013. Real and simulated events exceeded shuffles across a wide range of correlation and jump thresholds. PBEs needed 50 ms or longer and at least 5 cells.
limits: Place-field statistics only 'qualitatively similar, not quantitatively identical'. Shows sufficiency, not mechanism.
agent_relevance: Preplay-like order can arise from generic structure plus few cues. A weak structural prior may be enough; no stored plan library is needed.

source: Breffle et al. (2024) threshold-grid caveats
finding: The significance grids have built-in blind spots: the upper-right corner cannot be significant, and the leftmost column is underpowered because few events pass a strict jump-distance cut.
numbers: Same two statistics as Farooq et al. 2019 (absolute weighted correlation, max jump distance).
limits: Conclusions depend on threshold grid and shuffle type.
agent_relevance: Report which thresholds and null model support a claim.

source: Zhou, Sibille, Dragoi (2025) Generative emergence of non-local representations in the hippocampus
finding: Pro-preplay evidence from the original Dragoi lab. Theta sequences for a novel detour appeared within 1-2 laps by re-using sequence motifs seen in pre-detour sleep. Detour and old maps flickered on different theta phases.
numbers: Adult male rats. Theta sequences survived spike-time jitter of 35-55 ms that abolished phase precession (p=2.1e-11 at one jitter scale); detour laps 1-2 p=1.4e-4 after burst-only spike removal. Exact N rats not read.
limits: Same lab as the 2011 claim, not independent. Motifs are re-purposed, not fully new.
agent_relevance: A new route can be built quickly from old fragments. Supports a reusable library of sub-plans.

source: Denovellis et al. (2021) Hippocampal replay of experience at real-world speeds
finding: A state-space decoder finds most sharp-wave-ripple events carry coherent content, and many run at real-world speeds, not the usual 20x compressed speed. How rare replay looks depends on the decoder.
numbers: 10 rats. 96% (22,170 of 23,071) of classified SWRs and 86% (22,170 of 25,844) of all SWRs had spatially coherent structure. Only 14% (3,295 of 23,071) had any incoherent segment. Classification threshold 0.80 posterior. The most common class was slower than compressed replay.
limits: Reanalysis of existing data. Coherence is not proof of function.
agent_relevance: Detection method sets the apparent replay rate. Slow, stepwise rollouts may be the common mode.

source: Zheng, Hwaun, Loza, Colgin (2021) Hippocampal place cell sequences differ during correct and error trials in a spatial memory task
finding: Sequence quality tracks success. Correct trials showed longer, more compressed paths toward the goal. Rest-time replay was biased to paths ending at the correct reward location on correct but not error trials.
numbers: Running speed did not differ between correct and error trials (F(1,42)=1.2, p=0.3, partial eta2=0.03). Wait time before running did not differ (T(42)=0.6, p=0.5, d=0.1).
limits: Correlational. Look-ahead distance is partly confounded with stop distance.
agent_relevance: A weak plan leaves a trace before the action. A checker could flag a weak plan before execution.

source: Diekmann and Cheng (2023) A model of hippocampal replay driven by experience and environmental structure facilitates spatial learning
finding: A cheap replay rule (experience strength, similarity, inhibition of return) trains RL agents far better than random replay and comes close to the costly Mattar and Daw prioritised replay. Reverse mode matters most.
numbers: Escape latency over trials on linear track, open field, labyrinth. Reverse mode clearly beat no replay and random replay and was 'close to, even if slightly below' Mattar and Daw. Default mode only slightly better than random replay. No latency table read.
limits: Gridworld RL, not language tasks.
agent_relevance: Prioritised replay beats random replay, and a cheap heuristic gets most of the gain. Inhibition of return resembles a loop guard.

source: Antonov and Dayan (2025) Exploring replay
finding: Extends the Mattar and Daw replay theory to uncertain environments: replay is chosen to improve exploration in belief space. Gives testable predictions and a normative reading of reported exploratory replay and preplay.
numbers: Simulated Bayesian bandits and a spatial navigation task. No animal data, no effect sizes.
limits: Theory with no animal test yet.
agent_relevance: Offline thinking should target what is uncertain, not only what is known. Gives a rule for which branch to simulate.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2011) Preplay of future place cell sequences by hippocampal cellular assemblies
finding: Original preplay claim: sleep sequences before a novel track matched the order of place fields later formed on it.
numbers: Not opened (full text not retrievable). Exact counts not verified.
limits: Contested by Silva 2015; statistic and shuffle choices.
agent_relevance: The founding plan-before-action claim is not secure.

source: Dragoi and Tonegawa (2013) Distinct preplay of multiple novel spatial experiences in the rat
finding: Reported preplay for multiple novel tracks.
numbers: Capacity about 15 tracks, as quoted in Breffle 2024 (opened).
limits: Not opened directly.
agent_relevance: Many alternative futures may be pre-stored in parallel.

source: Foster and Wilson (2006) Reverse replay of behavioural sequences in hippocampal place cells during the awake state
finding: Awake rats replay the just-run path in reverse order at reward.
numbers: Not opened; numbers not verified.
limits: Linear track, few rats; not a plan.
agent_relevance: Reverse replay as credit assignment, matching Diekmann reverse-mode gain.

source: Pfeiffer and Foster (2013) Hippocampal place-cell sequences depict future paths to remembered goals
finding: Awake replay before movement in a 2D arena depicts paths to the remembered goal. Used as evidence for planning.
numbers: Not opened (page blocked); numbers not verified.
limits: Challenged by Gillespie 2021.
agent_relevance: Forward simulation to a goal before acting.

source: Gillespie et al. (2021) Hippocampal replay reflects specific past experiences rather than a plan for subsequent choice
finding: Title claim: replay content reflects past experience, not the plan for the next choice. Counter to a pure planning reading.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers claimed.
limits: Different task (W-track) from Pfeiffer and Foster; a boundary condition.
agent_relevance: Do not equate replay with a plan. Separate memory replay from lookahead.

source: Mattar and Daw (2018) Prioritized memory access explains planning and hippocampal replay
finding: RL theory: replay is ordered by gain times need. Explains reverse and forward replay.
numbers: Not opened. Diekmann 2023 (opened) says its cheaper rule is close in performance.
limits: Model; costly to compute.
agent_relevance: Ordering rule for rollouts: expected gain times need.

source: Grosmark and Buzsaki (2016) Diversity in neural firing dynamics supports both rigid and learned hippocampal sequences
finding: Reconciling account: rigid cells carry pre-existing order, plastic cells carry the learned part. Sequence is a mix.
numbers: Not opened (paywalled); no numbers claimed.
limits: Cell-type roles are hard to translate to LLMs.
agent_relevance: Split the scaffold into fixed prior routines and learned updates.

source: Farooq and Dragoi (2019) Emergence of preconfigured and plastic time-compressed sequences in early postnatal development
finding: Preconfigured sequences exist in young rats; experience-dependent sequences emerge later.
numbers: Not opened; numbers not verified.
limits: Developing animals; same lab as 2011.
agent_relevance: Prior structure first, learning later.

source: Whittington, Warren, Behrens (2022) Relating transformers to models and neural representations of the hippocampal formation
finding: Shows a mathematical link between transformers with recurrent position encodings and the Tolman-Eichenbaum Machine. Trained transformers develop grid-like and band-like codes. No test of preplay or replay.
numbers: Formal link; ICLR 2022. No replay measurement.
limits: No replay result; do not cite as LLM replay support.
agent_relevance: A structural analogy only.

source: HEMA: A Hippocampus-Inspired Extended Memory Architecture for Long-Context AI Conversations (2025)
finding: A compact summary plus vector store on a frozen 6B transformer lifts long-dialogue QA. It is hippocampus-inspired but has no replay. Authors say replay-style fine-tuning does not solve the prompt-budget limit.
numbers: Long-form QA accuracy 0.41 to 0.87. Recall after 150 turns 87%, +46 points over raw model and +25 over summary-only. 72% factual recall over 500 turns (250K tokens) vs raw model forgetting 80%. +0.18 s latency, 1.2 GB RAM for 50K vectors.
quote: replay alone does not solve prompt-budget limits
limits: Small model, own benchmark, no replay ablation. 'Inspired' is a design label.
agent_relevance: Retrieval of stored episodes helps long tasks. It is memory, not replay or preplay.

source: The Auton Agentic AI Framework (2026)
finding: A Reflector agent consolidates experience at session end and cites hippocampal replay as design basis. No replay-specific test found in the text.
numbers: No replay numbers found.
limits: Framework paper; analogy only.
agent_relevance: Offline consolidation between sessions is a common design with no test of replay-like gains.

source: Search sweep for LLM studies on replay or preplay (arXiv API plus 1 WebSearch, 2026-11-17)
finding: No LLM study was found that induces or measures preplay or replay and reports a result. Hits were architecture papers (HEMA, Auton, SLEEP, Active Dreaming Memory) and surveys.
numbers: Zero direct tests found; arXiv API returned nothing for replay plus LLM queries.
limits: Shallow search. SLEEP and Active Dreaming not opened.
agent_relevance: The LLM gap is real. Any scaffold use of replay is a hypothesis.
